headline: BOC Clark Intercepts ₱8.375 Million in Suspected Ketamine
seoTitle: BOC Clark Intercepts ₱8.375 Million in Suspected Ketamine
seoDescription: Customs and anti-drug officers intercepted about 1,675 grams of suspected ketamine concealed in a resin rabbit figurine at the Port of Clark.
deck: Customs and anti-drug officers intercepted about 1,675 grams of suspected ketamine concealed in a resin rabbit figurine at the Port of Clark.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Bureau of Customs-Port of Clark, the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency and the Clark Inter-Agency Task Force Against Illegal Drugs intercepted a parcel containing about 1,675 grams of suspected ketamine valued at ₱8.375 million.
The Bureau of Customs said the substance was concealed inside a resin rabbit figurine in a parcel from France that had been declared as an indoor decorative molded polyresin ornament.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: According to the bureau, the operation began with information from PDEA. A K-9 sniff test produced a positive indication, prompting a complete physical examination, while initial screening with a Rigaku spectrometer indicated the presence of suspected ketamine.

Customs issued a warrant of seizure and detention for alleged violations of the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act in relation to the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act. The substance remains described as suspected ketamine pending the applicable confirmatory and legal processes.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The interception shows how narcotics can be concealed in ordinary-looking parcels and why coordination among customs, police and drug-enforcement agencies matters at ports of entry.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for confirmatory laboratory results, any identified respondents and formal charges. No consignee is named in this report.
